_meta.indication: ISTURISA is a cortisol synthesis inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed FDA documents
pivotal_trials.design: 48-week multicenter study (Core Period) with a 12-week open-label dose titration, a 12-week open-label maintenance, an 8-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized withdrawal period (which provided the primary endpoint data), and an open-label Period 4.
pivotal_trials.population: Cushing's disease patients with persistent or recurrent disease despite pituitary surgery, or de novo patients for whom surgery was not indicated or who refused surgery; mean age 41 years, 77% female.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: percentage of complete responders (mUFC ≤ ULN) at the end of the 8-week randomized withdrawal period (Week 34), comparing continued ISTURISA versus placebo.
pivotal_trials.n: 137 patients received ISTURISA in Period 1; 71 responders were randomized 1:1 at Week 26 to continue ISTURISA (n=36) or switch to placebo (n=35).
pivotal_trials.result: At end of Period 3, complete responder rate was 86% (ISTURISA) vs 29% (placebo); difference 57% (95% CI 38, 76); 2-sided p<0.001. Key secondary complete responder rate at Week 24 was 52.6% (95% CI 43.9, 61.1).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>10%) in the 48-week study (N=137) were adrenal insufficiency (43.1%), fatigue (38.7%), nausea (37.2%), headache (30.7%), edema (21.2%), and nasopharyngitis (19.7%). Key risks include hypocortisolism, QT prolongation, and accumulation of adrenal hormone precursors/androgens.
target_moa: Osilodrostat is a cortisol synthesis inhibitor that inhibits 11β-hydroxylase (CYP11B1), the enzyme responsible for the final step of cortisol biosynthesis in the adrenal gland; it also inhibits aldosterone synthase.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held for this application; outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues warranting discussion.

description.text: Broadened indication to include treatment of adult patients with Cushing's syndrome (hypercortisolism) for whom surgery is not an option or has not been curative

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for broadening the indication of osilodrostat to include the treatment of patients with Cushing's syndrome, for a proposed single combined indication for the treatment of adult patients with Cushing's syndrome (hypercortisolism) for whom surgery is not an option or has not been curative.

description.text: Updated Prescribing Information based on final Phase 3 Trial C2302 results and added safety updates on febrile neutropenia (no new indication)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for updates to the Prescribing Information based on the final results of Clinical Trial C2302 entitled, "A Phase 3, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, 48 week study with an initial 12 week placebo-controlled period to evaluate the safety and efficacy of osilodrostat in patients with Cushing's disease", as well as safety updates on febrile neutropenia. In addition, the Patient Package Insert was revised to improve safe use of the product.

orphan_indication.text: Osilodrostat was granted Orphan Drug designation for the treatment of Cushing's disease on 9/13/2013.

citations.quote: Osilodrostat was granted Orphan Drug designation for “the treatment of Cushing’s disease” on 9/13/2013 by the Office of Orphan Products Development.

summary.text: This was a standard (not priority) review of a 505(b)(1) NDA received March 7, 2019, approved on the basis of a single pivotal randomized-withdrawal Phase 3 trial (C2301). The product had Orphan Drug designation for Cushing's disease; approval was a traditional (non-accelerated) approval with a postmarketing requirement to complete Phase 3 trial C2302. No advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: On March 7, 2019 Novartis submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) for osilodrostat under Section 505(b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for the following indication:
Osilodrostat was granted Orphan Drug designation for “the treatment of Cushing’s disease” on 9/13/2013 by the Office of Orphan Products Development.

requirement.text: 3816-1: Complete Clinical Trial C2302, a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, 48-week study with an initial 12-week placebo-controlled period to evaluate the safety and efficacy of osilodrostat in Cushing's disease patients, including occurrence of hypocortisolism and adrenal insufficiency.

citations.quote: 3816-1 Complete Clinical Trial C2302, a Phase 3, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, 48-week study with an initial 12-week placebo-controlled period to evaluate the safety and efficacy of osilodrostat in patients with Cushing's disease. Safety evaluations include but are not limited to the occurrence of hypocortisolism and adrenal insufficiency.
